ei.title: Seeds as the Best Survival Strategy
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Plants are amazing. Throughout their long existence, they have created diverse survival strategies. Seeds, in particular, are one of the strongest survival techniques they have developed. Let's discover the fascinating and mysterious world of seeds. Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world's largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals' digestive tracts untouched. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds. Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. Devil's claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil's claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. Its blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals. As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them feel like the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws. That is how devil's claw became known as the worst free rider. Out of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground to eat or lay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size. Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it were antelope dung. That is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot. They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls. By tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better. Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to elevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds. As a result, it can travel much farther from the parent tree. The rotation also slows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps reduce the damage to the seed during the fall. In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently concealed in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided that there is fire.

When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① distributing: 전치사 for 뒤 동명사로 알맞음

✅ ② that: 선행사 a sweet smell을 받는 주격 관계대명사로 알맞음

❌ ③ eating → to eat: 'It tempts animals to eat'은 'tempt + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문이므로 to eat이 맞음 ← 정답

✅ ④ digested: 'is digested'로 수동태를 이루어 알맞음

Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, ③<u>spreading</u> them without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are ④<u>equipping</u> with sharp hooks or needles. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ equipping → equipped: 'be equipped with' 수동태
det.analysis:
✅ ① to scatter: 'opt to + 동사원형' 구문으로 알맞음

✅ ② providing: 전치사 by 뒤 동명사로 알맞음

✅ ③ spreading: 분사구문(동시동작)으로 알맞음

❌ ④ equipping → equipped: 씨앗이 갈고리로 '갖춰진' 것이므로 'are equipped with'의 수동태가 맞음 ← 정답

questions.passage: Maple seeds are ①<u>shaped</u> like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed ②<u>to stay</u> in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② to stay → stay: 'make + 목적어 + 동사원형'
det.analysis:
✅ ① shaped: 'are shaped like'로 수동태를 이루어 알맞음

❌ ② to stay → stay: 'makes the seed stay'는 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형 구문이므로 stay가 맞음 ← 정답

✅ ③ caused: 'The rotation (which is) caused by'로 과거분사 수식으로 알맞음

✅ ④ to elevate: 'allow + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문으로 알맞음
det.tip: 사역동사 make + O + 동사원형 / allow + O + to부정사

det.korean: ③ containing → contain: 절의 정동사 필요
det.analysis:
✅ ① bound: 'are bound together'로 수동태를 이루어 알맞음

✅ ② protected: 'are securely protected'로 수동태로 알맞음

❌ ③ containing → contain: 'because the leaves ___ highly flammable oil'에서 접속사 because가 이끄는 절의 정동사가 필요하므로 contain이 맞음 ← 정답

✅ ④ which: 앞 절 전체를 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 알맞음

det.korean: ④ disappointing → satisfying: '만족스러운' 식사

✅ ① digested: 과육이 동물에게 '소화된다'는 문맥에 적절

✅ ② untouched: 씨앗은 '훼손되지 않은' 채 소화관을 통과한다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ③ sprout: 씨앗이 '싹트고' 자란다는 문맥에 적절

❌ ④ disappointing(실망스러운) → satisfying(만족스러운): 동물이 '만족스러운' 식사의 대가로 씨앗을 퍼뜨리므로 satisfying이 맞음 ← 정답

questions.passage: As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals. det.korean: ② gathered → scattered: 씨앗이 '흩어진다'
det.analysis:
✅ ① attached: 갈고리가 열매를 털에 '붙어 있게' 한다는 문맥에 적절

❌ ② gathered(모이는) → scattered(흩어지는): 동물이 이동하면 씨앗이 여러 장소에 '흩어지므로' scattered가 맞음 ← 정답

✅ ③ severe: 갈고리가 '심한' 통증을 유발한다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ④ horrifying: '섬뜩한' 발톱으로 할퀴는 것 같다는 문맥에 적절

det.analysis:
본문에 'the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals' digestive tracts untouched'라고 나와 있다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① without any return benefit(아무런 보답 없이)
det.analysis:
jackfruit처럼 먹이를 주는 식물과 달리, 어떤 식물은 동물에게 씨앗을 붙여 '아무런 보답 없이' 퍼뜨린다는 대조의 흐름이다.

✅ without any return benefit: 보답 없이 이용한다는 문맥 ← 정답

❌ in exchange for sweet food(달콤한 먹이의 대가로)는 보답을 주는 경우라 반대

❌ to protect the weak animals·after a very long journey는 문맥과 무관

det.korean: ④ stay in the air longer and fly farther(공중에 더 오래 머물고 더 멀리 날아간다)
det.analysis:
바로 뒤에서 회전이 씨앗을 '두 배 더 높이 올라가게(elevate twice as high)' 하고 '모체 나무로부터 훨씬 더 멀리 이동하게' 한다고 하므로, 회전은 씨앗을 더 오래·멀리 날게 한다.

✅ stay in the air longer and fly farther ← 정답

❌ sink straight to the ground·stop spinning right away·break into many small pieces는 회전의 이점과 반대이거나 무관

questions.passage: Plants are amazing. Throughout their long existence, they have created diverse survival strategies. Seeds, in particular, are one of the strongest survival techniques they have developed. Let's discover the fascinating and mysterious world of seeds. Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world's largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals' digestive tracts untouched. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.

questions.passage: Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to elevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds. As a result, it can travel much farther from the parent tree. The rotation also slows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps reduce the damage to the seed during the fall. In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience.
